H1.title: H1 — Deprivation Friction
H1.details: Socio-economic context significantly explains deprivation variance driven by basic service access and informal housing. Tent-served VDs experience a within-ward participation penalty of -1.00 pp (up to -3.12 pp in extreme clusters). Water access and refuse deprivation strongly depress voter participation.

H2.title: H2 — Incumbency Demobilisation
H2.details: Dominance does NOT uniformly depress turnout. In DA strongholds, a 1 SD larger margin boosts turnout by +0.41 SD (strong mobilization). In ANC wards, the margin effect is flat (+0.05 SD, p=0.58). Disaffection manifests as disengagement (staying home) rather than defection to opposition parties.

shapiro_wilk.note: Mild non-normality; rank-based and robust methods justified

mann_whitney_metro.note: No statistically significant turnout difference between JHB (42.1%) and TSH (41.1%)

kruskal_wallis_party.note: Overwhelming party-stronghold turnout divergence (ANC 39.4% vs DA 51.7%)

vif_audit.note: OLS excluded due to multicollinearity (VIF > 10); Ridge chosen by one-SE rule
